blocks.x: Retention on a governed propensity stack, involuntary churn down 40% and save-offer efficiency up 34%
Identity withheld, a mobile operator whose retention budget went to customers who asked loudest rather than those who mattered most. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline quarter priced the shouting: save offers triggered by cancellation calls, 61% of offers landing on customers who would have stayed anyway, and involuntary churn, billing failures, SIM swaps, unmanaged entirely.
Propensity models existed in a vendor tool nobody retrained. Their scores decayed quietly while the save desk worked the list they produced two quarters ago.

We rebuilt retention as a platform suite: churn signals from network, billing and care resolved into one propensity model retrained monthly with evaluation gates, involuntary-churn causes fixed at source (payment retries, eSIM flows), and save offers sequenced by customer lifetime with the contact policy enforced by the platform. The loudest customer stopped being the strategy.
